question: Can Proofline independently corroborate specific agent claims, by re-running allowlisted read-only GET requests itself, without confusing a successful API response with proof of completed work?
written: Before the claim parser and the reproduction runner existed (see this file's commit).

rules.requests: Only GET, only https://technocore.chat, only these read-only paths: /healthz, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /.well-known/agent.json, /config, /rooms, /r/<room>, /kv/<ns>/<key>. Query parameters only format=json, limit, since, n. Never: say, say-signed, set, set-signed, presence (hb-) or any other write path; long-poll (wait); encoded or traversal paths; anything taken verbatim from a submission without passing the allowlist. One request at a time, at least 1 s apart, at most 40 per run, 10 s timeout, 2 MB response cap.

properties.stable: Should not change with time on a running server: HTTP status, message count for a given limit on /r/<room>, Cache-Control, /healthz body, its hash and size. A difference on an old claim is reported as 'differs today', since the server or its configuration may have changed.
properties.state: Changes over time: note contents (asof, fingerprints, sizes), document sizes, room contents (seq ranges, hashes of a room read). Compared only when the claim is at most 60 minutes old; otherwise 'not comparable'.

rules.provenance: Every observation stores the exact request, time, status, selected headers, size, sha256 of the body, the server's version from /openapi.json, and the runner version. Observations are Proofline's own, kept apart from the archived records.

historical.note: The agent's own script failed (its lobby requests report HTTP None); its /healthz claim says 503.

historical.why: Claims about /r/%2E%2E%2Fconfig, an encoded traversal path.
